event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: KHC’s 2024 Form 10-K still frames COVID-19 primarily as an ongoing but attenuating, forward-looking risk rather than an acute, quantified hit.  The company explicitly connects global or local pandemics—including COVID-19—to three broad impact channels: (i) demand volatility and retailer behaviour that can strain its supply chain, (ii) workforce illness that can halt production or disrupt suppliers, and (iii) potential litigation arising from pandemic-related corporate actions.  These references are specific enough to indicate real exposure (naming COVID-19 and detailing operational and legal pathways) yet remain largely qualitative with no monetary figures or probability statements.  Because the filing date (Feb 2024) is roughly four years after WHO declared COVID-19 a pandemic, the Time-Decay Principle dictates that individual risk-evidence scores fall in a moderate band (4-6 for the strongest items, 1-3 for weaker, more generic mentions).  Overall, the pandemic is still judged material but no longer an immediate crisis, so the evidence reflects a medium residual risk level.

evidence_list.snippet: Moreover, weak economic conditions, recessions, inflation, severe or unusual weather events, global or local pandemics, including COVID-19, as well as other factors, could affect consumer preferences and demand, at times, causing a strain on our supply chain due, in part, to retailers, distributors, or carriers modifying their restocking, fulfillment, or shipping practices.

components.reason: Explicitly cites ‘global or local pandemics, including COVID-19’.
Links pandemic to both consumer-demand shifts and supply-chain strain.
Language is conditional and grouped with many other macro factors (generic, unquantified).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct COVID-19 reference with concrete supply-chain and demand pathways, but generic wording and no quantification keep it to a moderate 4.

evidence_list.snippet: Furthermore, actions we have taken or may take, or decisions we have made or may make, in response to pandemics (including the COVID-19 pandemic), may result in investigations, legal claims, or litigation against us.

components.reason: Names COVID-19 explicitly and ties it to potential legal exposure.
Highly speculative (‘may’) and lacks operational or financial detail.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Adds a legal-liability angle but is speculative and unquantified, so it scores a modest 2.

evidence_list.snippet: Illness of our workforce, or the workforce of third parties with which we do business, due to influenza or pandemics, could disrupt production of our products in one or more of our manufacturing facilities, or cause our suppliers, vendors, distributors, or third-party manufacturers to fail to meet their obligations to us.

components.reason: Describes direct operational disruption (production shutdown, supplier failure).
Places pandemics as causal factor affecting both internal and external labour.
Uses generic ‘pandemics’ (COVID-19 implied but not named) and presents risk conditionally.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Strong operational detail but less specificity (COVID-19 not named here), yielding a solid mid-level score of 4.

evidence_list.snippet: Such events and circumstances could include a sustained decrease in our market capitalization, increased competition or unexpected loss of market share, increased input costs beyond projections, disposals of significant brands or components of our business, unexpected business disruptions (for example due to a natural disaster, pandemic, or loss of a customer, supplier, or other significant business relationship), unexpected significant declines in operating results, significant adverse changes in the markets in which we operate, changes in income tax rates, changes in interest rates, or changes in management strategy.

components.reason: Lists ‘pandemic’ as a trigger for business disruptions that could drive asset impairment.
Very broad catch-all list, no COVID-19 reference, highly generic.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Pandemic is only one item in a long generic list with no specificity; after offsets, the snippet carries negligible incremental risk (score 0).
